Overview

Rambus, a premier chip and silicon IP provider making data faster and safer, is seeking to hire an exceptional Product Engineering Intern to join our NPI Product Engineering team in San Jose, CA. In this role, you will be working with some of the brightest inventors and engineers in the world developing products that make data faster and safer.

As a Summer 2027 Product Engineering Intern, you’ll play a pivotal role in supporting our New Product Introduction (NPI) engineering data automation and test time reduction efforts for Rambus memory interface chip products. In this full-time, 12-week summer role, you’ll report directly to our Senior Manager, Product Engineering. Our NPI Product Engineering team is dedicated to bridging product development and high-volume manufacturing by driving test, yield, quality, and manufacturing readiness for new products, and your contributions will be instrumental in migrating legacy ATE NPI test data into our Silicon.DA engineering data platform and enabling data-driven test time reduction.

Rambus offers a flexible work environment, embracing a hybrid approach for most office-based roles. Employees are encouraged to spend an average of at least three days per week onsite, allowing for two days of remote work.

Responsibilities

- Migrate legacy ATE NPI test data into Silicon.DA, our central NPI engineering data platform, including data cleanup, formatting, and validation of completeness and accuracy.

- Collect and organize test time data from ATE test programs to support test time reduction activities.

- Analyze test time and yield data by test, insertion, and product to help identify test time reduction opportunities, and summarize findings for the engineering team.

- Develop scripts (e.g., Python or SQL) to automate data extraction, ingestion, and reporting.

- Document data structures, workflows, and procedures so the work can be sustained after the internship.

- Collaborate with Product, Test, and IT engineering teams, and present a final project summary at the end of the internship.

Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field, and returning to school after the internship.

- Programming experience in Python and/or SQL for data processing and analysis.

- Strong data analysis skills; experience with Excel, JMP, or similar data analysis tools.

- Basic understanding of semiconductor devices and test concepts; exposure to ATE, test data formats (e.g., STDF), or semiconductor manufacturing is a plus.

- Strong attention to detail, organization, and written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to work independently and as part of a cross-functional team.

- Available to work full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 weeks during Summer 2027 in San Jose, CA.

About Rambus

Rambus is a global company that makes industry-leading memory interface chips and Silicon IP to advance data center connectivity and solve the bottleneck between memory and processing. With over 30 years of semiconductor experience, we are a leading provider of high-performance products and innovations that maximize the bandwidth, capacity and security for AI and other data-intensive workloads. Our world-class team is the foundation of our company, and our innovative spirit drives us to develop the cutting-edge products and technologies essential for tomorrow’s systems.

Rambus offers a competitive compensation package including base salary, bonus, equity, matching 401(k), employee stock purchase plan, comprehensive medical and dental benefits, time-off program, and gym membership.

The US hourly range for this full-time position is $25.80 to $47,80. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location. The successful candidate’s starting pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions.

We value a range of perspectives and experiences that contribute to innovation and collaboration. Our goal is to ensure that all team members have equitable access to opportunities, resources, and a sense of belonging. We believe that a culture of fairness and inclusion helps us all do our best work.

Rambus is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About the Role & Team

Bedrock's Product team decides what our autonomous machines should learn to do next. We also make sure the people who work alongside them get real value from them: operators, site managers and the construction companies we partner with. Our problems rarely arrive as specs. Which task or machine type is worth taking on next? How do you turn "digs like an expert" into a number you can measure? What does a partner need to see before trusting a 40-ton machine on their site?

As our Product intern, you'll get a problem like that, not a task list, and own it for the summer. You'll frame it, work out the answer, build what's needed, and bring the team a recommendation they can act on. You'll work the way our team does: with AI tools in hand, going from question to working prototype in days, not weeks.

What You'll Do

- Own an open product problem end to end: frame it, find the data and the people who know, decide what to build, and ship it before the summer ends

- Turn fleet data from real jobsites into decisions: how well our machines perform, where they struggle, and what that means for what we build next

- Prototype with AI coding tools and agents: internal tools, data pipelines, automated workflows, and working demos that make an idea concrete instead of slides about it

- Spend time at our field sites with operators and site teams, and turn what you see into requirements engineers can build against

- Work across autonomy, evaluation, operations and commercial teams to pressure-test ideas and unblock yourself

- Write up your findings and present a clear recommendation to leadership: what you found, what you built, and what we should do next

What We're Looking For

Required

- Currently pursuing a BS or MS in computer science, engineering, math, economics or another technical or quantitative field, or bringing equivalent experience building things

- A track record of agency: you've taken on a problem nobody assigned you (a project, a tool, a company, a research question) and carried it to a real result

- AI-native: you use tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex every day to build, analyze and write, and you know how to check their output and when not to trust it

- Hands-on with data: Python or SQL, plus comfort reading code and following a technical discussion with engineers

- Clear, concise writing: you can turn a messy problem into a one-page recommendation someone can act on

- Willingness to spend time at our field sites, in PPE, around heavy equipment

Preferred

- Something you built that real people use: an app, an internal tool, an open-source project, a startup

- Prior product, engineering or founding-team experience at a startup

- Experience with robotics, autonomy, ML or data-heavy products

- Interest in construction or other physical-world industries; no prior experience needed

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

ABOUT THE JOB

Maritime Digital Production builds the digital systems behind Anduril's maritime build chain: data pipelines, contextualization layers, workflow and execution tools, applied intelligence, and the interfaces between OT and IT. Everything we build has to survive production constraints, which means real crews, real equipment, and real disruption.

Raw data off the factory floor doesn't mean much on its own. A tag reading PLC4_TT_1142 tells you nothing until someone establishes that it's a temperature sensor, on a specific machine, in a specific cell, measuring a specific process step. Doing that for thousands of signals is a cataloging problem before it's an engineering one.

That's the job. You'll build the vocabularies, hierarchies, and metadata standards that give factory data meaning, working alongside data engineers and manufacturing engineers who need the structure and don't have the training to build it.
If you like building a taxonomy and want to see one used somewhere other than a library, this is that.

- Develop and maintain controlled vocabularies for equipment, materials, processes, and locations across the build chain.

- Build asset hierarchies and naming conventions that structure plant-floor data into a consistent model.

- Write and apply metadata schemas for industrial data sources, documenting what each field means and how it should be used.

- Catalog data sources and maintain entries in the team's data catalog, including provenance and ownership.

- Audit existing tags and data models for inconsistency and gaps and propose corrections.

- Present your work to the team at the end of the session.
